subject.title: [Feature]: Gateway-lite mode without an AI harness for deterministic deployments

question: Should OpenClaw support a first-class no-harness control-plane deployment, and if so should it be delivered through the broader gateway/runtime process split or a separately packaged gateway profile?
rationale: Plugins can short-circuit model turns, but they cannot prove that agent runtime code and credentials are absent; selecting the permanent process, packaging, security, and compatibility boundary requires maintainer intent.

options.title: Unify with runtime split
options.body: Make the lightweight gateway/control plane from https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/42026 the canonical architecture and add deterministic plugin execution as an explicit control-plane capability.

options.title: Create a gateway profile
options.body: Keep the embedded architecture but publish a separately built and validated profile that excludes agent-harness modules and AI credential paths.

options.title: Limit scope to plugin interception
options.body: Decline an artifact-level boundary and document before_agent_reply plus direct tool invocation as the supported deterministic pattern, acknowledging that harness code remains installed.

recommendation.title: Unify with runtime split
recommendation.body: Make the lightweight gateway/control plane from https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/42026 the canonical architecture and add deterministic plugin execution as an explicit control-plane capability.

likelyOwner.reason: They merged the central deterministic interception seam and have adjacent provider-runtime boundary history.
